I've been working this land for 40 years. I know what works. My body isn't as strong as it was, and there's only me to do the work, so I keep things manageable.

My main income is stevia — that's why I center my system around it. The buyers come to collect, the price is decent, and I know the crop. I'll put 7 mu into stevia on the better-drained parcels. It needs more watering and weeding than wheat, but I manage.

The other 8 mu I run the usual wheat-maize rotation like everyone around here. Wheat goes in October after I finish the maize harvest. Maize goes back in June after wheat. Same land, twice a year. I've done this my whole life.

For seeds — I buy hybrid maize from the village supply station, everyone does, the yields are much better. For wheat I use the improved variety I've been using for years, works well on my soil. For stevia I keep my own root cuttings from last year, saves money.

Fertilizer I apply the way my father taught me and what I've adjusted over the decades. I add a bit more nitrogen on the maize because the summer heat demands it. I'm careful not to over-water the stevia — I've seen roots rot when neighbors got greedy with irrigation.

I do two pesticide passes on each crop. Aphids on wheat, corn borer on maize, and leaf disease on stevia — same problems every year.
